The call

You are answering "what is this made of". The class drives two different systems. It sets metallic for shading — and metallic means the surface answers light differently (no diffuse, specular tinted by the albedo, sheen at grazing angles), not that you can see yourself in it. It also picks the impact effect: a bullet into metal throws sparks, into concrete it throws dust and chips, into water a splash. Sparks currently fire on everything that is not flesh, liquid or sky, which is why concrete needs its own call — and the liquid test only knows about flats the map marks as liquid, so a wall of falling blood needs fluid saying so. Doom 64 is mostly painted steel, cast iron, worn plate and grating — nearly all of it metal and rough. Reach for rough and leave the mirror bucket for the handful of surfaces that earn it.

Roughness

Highlight this roughness gives, tinted by the texture's own colour.

RTGL1 renders water and lava as media (RG_MESH_PRIMITIVE_WATER / LAVA), not through this BRDF. On a fluid texture the roughness pick is mostly cosmetic — take the obvious one and move on.

Set roughness first, then call it. Pressing S on its own means metal at 0.80 — the common case costs one key.

Working set

Pick a map to label just that map first, apply it, and look at the result in game before committing to all 1345. The two filters compose, so MAP01 + metal is how you re-check a batch after seeing it. Everything — arrows, ␣, the strip, the counter — stays inside the set. Labels stay put when you clear a filter; they are never scoped to one.

Export

Exports everything you have labelled by default, filter or no filter — the applier should never have to guess at scope. Saved to this browser on every keystroke. Downloads are blocked in this viewer, so copy the JSON out — paste it back into the box to resume on another machine.
